## 1. Valuation & Yield Measures

- **Internal Rate of Return (IRR)**  
  The discount rate that make net PV today (NPV) zero.
- **Yield to Maturity {YTM}**  
  IRR of a bond.  
  Bond price is observed in the market & ytm is implied from it.

$$
  \mathrm{NPV}=0\;\Rightarrow\;\mathrm{Price}=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\frac{\mathrm{Coupon}_i}{(1+\mathrm{ytm})^i}+\frac{1000+\mathrm{coupon}}{(1+\mathrm{ytm})^n}
  

$$
- YTM is quoted as an annualized rate  
  → It is annualized return that we will get if we hold the bond till maturity & do not sell in between.
- **Price Vs Value**  
  Price: the price at which the bond is trading right now. Decided by market  
  Value: the fair price of the bond decided by mathematical pricing formula
- If Price > Value ⇒ Bond is Overvalued.
- If Price < Value ⇒ Bond is cheap.
- **Dirty Price / Cash Price / Full Price** → Includes accrued interest.
- **Clean Price / Flat Price**: Dirty Price - accrued interest

## 2. Bond Trading Relationships

**Bond trading at:**

1. **Discount:** PV < FV; YTM > coupon ⇒ Similar bonds in market are giving greater YTM than this bond's coupon.
2. **Premium:** PV > FV; YTM < coupon
3. **Par:** PV = FV; YTM = coupon (At the time of issuing, bond is always issued at par.)

\* A bond with no coupon i.e ZCB always trades at discount i.e PV < FV & hence these are called discount bonds.

## 3. Spot Rates & Par Rates

**Spot rate** → Actually observed in market via ZCB (liquid product)

$$
\mathrm{DF}_i=\frac{1}{(1+S_i)^i}
$$

| ZCB | Purchase Price | DFi | Spot |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 yr | 980 | 0.980 | 2.04% |
| 2 yr | 945 | 0.945 | 2.87% |
| 3 yr | 901 | 0.901 | 3.533% |

spot rate ≡ YTM of a ZCB

$$
\mathrm{Coupon\ Bond\ PV}=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\frac{C_i}{(1+S_i)^i}+\frac{1000+C_n}{(1+S_n)^n}
$$

**Par rate:** Single flat coupon rate that makes a bond price exactly at Par. (given the spot rates are known)

$$
1000=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}C\cdot\mathrm{DF}_i+(1000+C)\mathrm{DF}_n
$$

[Find this flat coupon rate]

**For a ZCB:** Par rate = YTM = Coupon

## 4. Forward Rates & FRAs

**Forward Rate (fm,n):** loan starts at mth year & goes on for next n-years i.e total duration is (m+n) years (m = expiry, n = maturity)

<img alt="Forward Rate Timeline" src="data:image/png;base64," style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block;margin:1rem auto;" />

Timeline illustration of spot rates (S5, S8) and forward rate (f5,3)

$$
(1+f_{m,n})^n=\frac{(1+S_{m+n})^{m+n}}{(1+S_m)^m}
$$

### Forward Rate Agreement (FRA)

→ Forward contract on Interest Rate (Derivative on underlying IR ⇒ we are not actually taking loan, instead just speculating/hedging)

FRA(6m, 3m): 6 × 9 | FRA+ ⇒ Buyer, FRA- ⇒ Seller

E.g. Spot rate (6m) = 5.8%, agreed rate = 5% ⇒ Buyer makes profit of 0.8%

<img alt="FRA 6m, 3m Timeline" src="data:image/png;base64," style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block;margin:1rem auto;" />

FRA (6m, 3m) Settlement & Cash Flow Timeline

$$
\mathrm{FRA}^{+}\;\mathrm{payoff}=\mathrm{Notional}\cdot[0.8\%]\cdot\left[\frac{3\,\mathrm{m}}{12\,\mathrm{m}}\right]=100\,\mathrm{M}\cdot\frac{0.8}{100}\cdot\frac{3}{12}=0.2\,\mathrm{million}
$$

There is no cash exchanged at t=0 i.e when contract is drawn ⇒ Price of FRA is zero, Value ≠ 0.

**Synthetic FRA:** When we calculate forward rate, we need not draw an actual FRA contract; we first assume such a contract exists.

## 5. Spreads

**g-spread** = YTMcorp - YTMgovt  
→ term structure ko flat assume karke just diff corporate bond ke yield with govt (treasury bond)

**Z-spread:** ZCB yield ko parallel shift kando to find c-bond yield. Assumes non-flat term structure but adds a fixed number to all maturities.

## 6. Futures & Stock Forward Contracts

**Future:** Exchange traded (Future is on the floor). Marked to market ⇒ cash settled daily ⇒ **Value of future at any given time is zero.**

- **IM:** Initial margin (percentage of contract size)
- **MM:** Maintenance margin (minimum balance that must be maintained by any side / both)

### Forward Contract on Stock

F+: Contract to buy at F | F-: Contract to sell at F

| Condition | F+ (Buyer) | F- (Seller) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ST > F | Right to buy | Obligation to sell |
| ST < F | Obligation to buy | Right to sell |

## 7. Duration & Sensitivity Analysis

Duration types: Macaulay's Duration, Modified Duration, Effective Duration [Unit: [Duration] = time]

### 1) Macaulay's Duration (MacD)

Average time in which investment is recovered.  
i.e. At MacD: Realised return = YTM at time of issuance ⇒ Reinvestment Risk = Price Risk.

<img alt="Macaulay Duration Risk Horizon" src="data:image/png;base64," style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block;margin:1rem auto;" />

Macaulay Duration: Point where Price Risk and Reinvestment Risk offset each other

$$
\mathrm{MacD}=\frac{\sum_i(\mathrm{PV}_i\cdot T_i)}{\mathrm{PV}},\qquad\mathrm{where}\quad\mathrm{PV}_i=\frac{C_i}{(1+\mathrm{YTM})^i}
$$

- **When time < MacD:** YTM ↑ses, Bond price ↓ses & coupon re-investment is still not big enough to balance loss in bond price ⇒ Hold the bond (RR < YTM).  
  YTM ↓ses, Bond price ↑ses & we do not have too many coupons to re-invest ⇒ Sell the bond (RR > YTM).
- **When time > MacD:** YTM ↑ses, Bond price ↓ses but coupons are getting re-invested at greater interest ⇒ Hold the bond (RR > YTM).  
  YTM ↓ses, Bond price ↑ses but coupons are getting re-invested at lower rate ⇒ Sell the bond (RR < YTM).

### 2) Effective Duration (ED)

$$
\mathrm{ED}=\frac{\%\,\Delta\,\mathrm{in\ Bond\ Price}}{\%\,\Delta\,\mathrm{in\ YTM}}
$$

<img alt="Effective Duration Price-Yield Curve" src="data:image/png;base64," style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block;margin:1rem auto;" />

Effective Duration Price-Yield Curve Sensitivity

$$
\mathrm{ED}\;\mathrm{at}\;\mathrm{YTM}_0=\frac{1}{P_0}\cdot\left[\frac{P_2-P_1}{2\cdot0.5\%}\right]\cdot100\%=\frac{1}{P_0}\cdot\frac{dP}{d\mathrm{YTM}}
$$

ED ≡ 1% YTM ke change ke kaaran Bond price me kitne percent ka change

### 3) Modified Duration (MD)

Same as ED for non-option embedded bond.

$$
\mathrm{MD}=\frac{\mathrm{MacD}}{1+\mathrm{YTM}/m}\approx\mathrm{ED}
$$

[for non-option bonds] [Connects MD to MacD]

\* For option-embedded bond, MacD is not defined (bcz no fixed maturity)

## 8. Factors Impacting Duration & Price Risk Metrics

| Factor | MacD | ED | MD | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Maturity ↑ | MacD ↑ | ED ↑ | MD ↑ | All three follow same pattern. They are essentially the same. |
| Coupon ↑ | MacD ↓ | ED ↓ | MD ↓ |
| YTM ↑ | MacD ↓ | ED ↓ | MD ↓ |

**PVBP (Price Value of a Basis Point):** Change in Bond Price for 1 BP (100 BP = 1% ⇒ 1 BP = 0.01%)

$$
\mathrm{PVBP}=\frac{\mathrm{Price}\times\mathrm{ED}}{100}
$$

**Dollar Duration (aka Money Duration):** Change in Bond Price Per 100 BP = 100 × PVBP = Price × ED

**DV01:** Change in Bond price for 1 BP ΔYTM ≈ PVBP = Dollar Duration / 100
